title: Log overruled objections and recheck them
statement: Record every review objection that was overruled, with its reasoning, and check it again in the next round, so a recurrence counts as evidence rather than memory.
example: An objection overruled on 08-06 was raised independently by a later review on 08-11.
detail: The red-team skill for the reading course plans makes this its rule 14 and gives the case behind it: on 08-06 the team argued that a pre-filled quote inverts the release gradient, was told to implement it without pushback, and on 08-11 a later review raised the same point independently (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`). Without the log the earlier objection is only a memory; with it, it is calibration evidence for the next disagreement.

evidence.quote: When we raise an objection and are directed to proceed, record it with the reasoning.
Without the log that is a memory; with it, it is calibration evidence for the next disagreement.
one commit whose message records BOTH the fixed and the refuted-with-reasons lists.
